title: MOTR Pub
venue_description:
Over-the-Rhine's Original Music Laboratory

MOTR Pub has been presenting live original music and comedy in OTR since 2010 with shows six nights weekly. The venue focuses on new artist development both locally and globally creating fun atmosphere for music explorers and emerging artists.

Venue Spaces

Multiple performance areas including main room Sword Room and MOTR Patio allow different event types and crowd sizes. Professional sound engineers maintain top-of-line PA systems ensuring high-quality production values.

Weekly Music Events

Tuesday Open Mic (8 PM) - Original music only voted best open mic seven years running by City Beat readers. First-come first-served signup at 7:30 PM. Performers receive $2 off sandwiches. Some exceptions for covers possible (see host).

Monday Karaoke and Industry Night (8 PM-1 AM) - Kick Out The Jams karaoke plus industry networking.

Wednesday-Saturday Ticketed Concerts - Local regional and touring artists. MOTR was first Cincinnati appearance for Alabama Shakes Lord Huron Margo Price Twin Shadow.

Sunday Programming - Various events and special performances.

Food and Drink

Full menu with elevated pub fare craft beers cocktails non-alcoholic options. Kitchen stays open late accommodating both dinner-before-shows and post-performance meals.

Artist Development

Tuesday open mic serves as pathway to booking opportunities. Strong performers graduate from open mic to opening slots to headlining shows. Professional environment with maintained equipment experienced engineers allows artists to focus on performance not technical issues.

Sister Venue

Woodward Theater across street provides larger capacity for artists ready to graduate to bigger rooms. Established pathway from MOTR open mic to Woodward headliner.

Atmosphere

Equal parts music venue neighborhood bar and artistic incubator. Attracts serious music heads casual listeners industry professionals first-time concert-goers. Created fun exploratory atmosphere defining modern OTR.

title: The Comet
venue_description:
Northside's Eclectic Music and Burrito Haven

Northside Cincinnati's most eclectic beloved neighborhood bar combining great Mexican food impressive beer selection live music seven nights weekly. Features pool tables dart boards outdoor patio tiki bar sand volleyball court.

Atmosphere

Genuinely Northside vibe - unpretentious diverse creative slightly weird in best way. Kid-friendly during early hours especially Sunday bluegrass. Transitions to neighborhood hangout mode can become late-night party spot. Wonderfully diverse crowd includes families with kids hipsters bluegrass devotees neighborhood regulars.

Food

Exceptional Mexican fare - enormous burritos hot cheesy quesadilla platters fresh-made tacos famous salsa sampler (caution can be spicy). Generous portions extremely reasonable prices. Possible to enjoy several drink rounds and substantial food for bargain.

Drinks

Huge beer selection full cocktails outdoor tiki bar for seasonal tropical drinks. Don't open fridge yourself - bar staff will help.

Music Programming

Sunday Bluegrass - Comet Bluegrass All-Stars perform 7:30 PM and 9:00 PM shows. No cover charge. 25+ year tradition since 1996. Band has opened for Sam Bush Blue Highway Del McCoury Peter Rowan Ricky Skaggs.

Comedy Open Mic - Git Gud Comedy Open Mic 2nd and 4th Thursdays 7 PM in basement. No-pressure space for comics all experience levels. Hosted by rotating local comedians Gavin Ferckel Wayne Memmott Connor Twele Cody Walker.

Additional live music multiple nights weekly on varied schedule.

Other Activities

Sand volleyball leagues (contact knottypinevolley@gmail.com). Pool darts games available.

What Makes It Special

Charming dive bar pedigree with engaged audiences who actually listen. People come specifically for music not just drinking with background music. Comet crowds are knowledgeable appreciative especially for bluegrass. Complete experience - arrive early enjoy food drinks connect with artists and audience then experience quality performances. Part of Cincinnati tradition and music history spanning decades.

title: Leo Coffeehouse
venue_description:
Cincinnati's Folk and Americana Sanctuary

Operating since 1963 Leo Coffeehouse serves as listening room where quality of attention matches quality of performance. Run by all-volunteer Queen City Balladeers organization. Sunday evenings September through May at Zion United Church of Christ in Norwood.

Philosophy

Leo listening room is jewel of QCB and civic treasure. Musical oasis filled with attentive listeners. Quality of attention directly affects nature and quality of performance. Role of audience is as necessary to musical event as role of musician. All performances unpaid keeping it truly about the music.

Atmosphere

Caffeinated listening room (hence coffeehouse name) focused entirely on music. No bar service no food beyond coffee and snacks nothing to distract from primary purpose of sharing and experiencing acoustic music. Singular focus creates atmosphere unique in contemporary venues - come explicitly to listen not socialize over background music.

Sunday Schedule (5:15 PM start)

Every Sunday - Open jam in main hall where anyone can lead songs while others provide backup and harmony.

First Sundays - Rise Up Singalong 3 PM plus special workshops. Pick songs from Rise Up Singing and Rise Again songbooks. Led by Al Wauligman on piano.

Second Sundays - Songwriters Collaborative upstairs for sharing work receiving friendly critiques encouragement.

Third Sundays - Guitar Roundtable upstairs with Mike Helm. Forum for players any skill level to exchange ideas learn new licks and chords gain perspectives. Also features Open Mic starting 6:00 PM (sign up for 1-2 songs 8 minute limit).

Fourth Sundays - Old-Time Music Jam upstairs.

Evening Concerts

Scheduled performers take stage 6:40 PM to 9:00 PM every Sunday. Featured sets from talented local musicians performing folk Americana roots music. Quality performances in fine-sounding room create ideal setting for sharing music honing performance craft.

Admission

Guests welcome with voluntary donations. Annual memberships available for Leo series but not required. Keeping barrier to entry low ensures accessibility.

Musical Range

While steeped in Americana and folk traditions Leo welcomes all genres. Fingerstyle guitar wizardry traditional ballads contemporary songwriting old-time fiddle tunes all find home here.

For Performers

Rare opportunity to play for genuinely engaged audience in beautiful-sounding room where music treated as art not entertainment. Mistakes accepted as part of authentic performance. Focus entirely on music itself creates environment where artists can take risks grow develop craft.

History and Mission

Started 1963 by University of Cincinnati college students wanting venue for folk music. Originally in Clifton YMCA moved to Old St. George ten years ago more recently relocated to Zion UCC building. Continues mission of promoting roots and Americana music through volunteer dedication and community support.

title: Arnold's Bar and Grill
venue_description:
Ohio's Oldest Tavern and Living History

Open since 1861 Arnold's is Ohio's oldest continuously operated watering hole. Piece of living history where Civil War troops walked across floors unchanged from 1860s. Remained largely unaltered through 160+ years.

History

Occupies two buildings from 1838 originally barbershop and feed store. Simon Arnold converted to saloon 1861. Three generations of Arnolds lived in building over 98 years. During Prohibition operated as cafe allegedly producing moonshine in second-floor bathtub (bathtub still there). Wood and tile floors haven't been resurfaced since 1920s. Floor near entrance even older from 1860s. Tables date to 1910s clock from same era hangs over back bar.

National Recognition

Esquire Magazine Best Bars in America. Thrillist Most Iconic Bar in Ohio. The Daily Meal 150 Best Bars in America. City Beat Best Live Music While You Eat. Cincinnati Magazine Top 45 Burgers. Featured on Travel Channel Man v. Food Food Network Guy's Grocery Games Hot Ones with Padma Lakshmi. NBC Harry's Law built replica set of Arnold's.

The Courtyard

Opened 1976 beautiful performance space. Tented ceiling in winter open in summer always stunning. Stage hosts live music Tuesday through Saturday. Features mural with Emilio Estevez face (he's regular). Excellent acoustics natural enhancement with proper amplification for electric instruments.

Music Programming

Live music Tuesday-Saturday in courtyard. Wednesday Bluegrass Night featuring Tye Dye and other bands. Regular performances from local and touring artists. Most shows no cover charge. Historic venue with genuine significance - stage has hosted thousands of musicians over decades.

Food

Solid American fare with Cincinnati character. Greek spaghetti (spaghetti with olive oil butter garlic peppers onions mushrooms olives Romano cheese) is beloved signature dish. Arnold's famous meatballs served with red sauce over pasta shredded Romano. Burgers pastas chicken and waffles crab cakes. Vegetarian Cincinnati-style chili. Vegan options available. Generous portions acclaimed quality.

Drinks

Excellent beer selection including local craft breweries. Full bar wine by glass. 160+ years pouring drinks in this spot.

Atmosphere

Historic tavern character retained through original fixtures worn floors patina that can't be faked. Main bar warm historic lively - classic Cincinnati tavern. Courtyard provides beautiful setting for dining and performances.

For Musicians

Performing at Arnold's means participating in space with genuine historical significance. Built-in audience draws crowds for food drinks history - musicians reach people who might not specifically come for music but appreciate it. Regular programming Wednesday bluegrass residency consistent Tuesday-Saturday schedule. Tourism draw brings visitors from across country and world. Private events available (arnoldsparties@gmail.com) creating additional performance opportunities. Playing here means performing in Ohio's oldest tavern - authenticity earned through 160+ years serving community.

title: Fountain Square
venue_description:
Downtown Cincinnati's Premier Public Space

Cincinnati's central gathering place hosting free concerts community events throughout year. JAMII (Swahili for Community) weekly Wednesday program curated by Siri Imani provides platform for local performers and youth musicians.

JAMII Community Musical Night

Wednesday evenings 6-9 PM featuring two local Cincinnati performers. Youth 18 and younger take mic 7-8 PM. Professional sound system provided. Free admission no tickets required. All events brought by Fifth Third Bank.

Other Programming

Sunday Sounds free concerts. Jazz at the Park presented by Cincinnati Symphony Orchestra. Fifth and Vinyl events. UC College-Conservatory of Music performances. Seasonal programming including Winterhaus.

Location and Access

520 Vine Street downtown Cincinnati. Easily accessible public square. Family-friendly all-ages programming. Open to public for all events.

title: The Vault Mt Lookout
venue_description:
Mt Lookout Music Venue

Hosts Keep it Open Cincy weekly open mic Wednesdays 7-10 PM. Music and comedy performances in welcoming atmosphere. Great food and drinks menu. Layout perfect for performances. No cover or entry fee.

Programming

Wednesday Keep it Open Cincy open mic. Sign up early for performance slots. Full PA system provided. Supportive environment for musicians and comedians developing craft.

title: Knotty Pine Bar
venue_description:
West Side Live Music Staple

West side neighborhood bar featuring live music seven nights weekly. Pool tables dart boards large outdoor patio full-service tiki bar sand volleyball court. 30+ years serving community.

Music

Live acoustic Wednesday and Thursday. Full bands Friday-Saturday 9 PM-1 AM. Open mic nights. Everything from classic rock covers to blues to modern experiments. Lots of open space for dancing.

Atmosphere

Casual neighborhood bar vibe. Extended happy hours. Sand volleyball leagues. Elvis Pinball putt-putt arcade. Family-friendly environment. Private events welcome - birthdays corporate events fantasy drafts.

title: Go Bananas Comedy Club
venue_description:
Cincinnati Comedy Destination

Premier comedy club featuring national touring acts and local talent development. Wednesday $5 comedy open mic nights provide platform for emerging comedians.

Programming

Wednesday open mic nights $5 admission. National touring headliners regular schedule. Local comics development opportunities. Professional comedy club atmosphere with full food and drink service.
